name: Container freight
summary: Drewry container index eased 1% to $4,389 per 40ft on 5 Nov, still above the $4,000 Alert line
state: Drewry's World Container Index was $4,389 per 40ft container on 5 Nov, down 1% on the week and 124% above a year earlier (Shipping Telegraph; Breakbulk). Shanghai–New York fell 3% to $9,303 and Shanghai–Rotterdam 2% to $3,615. About 60% of Asia–Europe capacity now uses the Suez Canal, and Drewry flags Hormuz as a separate risk. The index remains above the $4,000 Alert line.
for_you: Importers and retailers face higher delivery costs and uncertain arrival times. These costs tend to reach shop prices after a lag of some months.
basis_detail: Drewry World Container Index / Freightos Baltic Index
basis_by: Drewry World Container Index / Freightos Baltic Index

why: Container rates feed through to goods prices months later; spikes are an early inflation and supply-chain warning.
drivers: Chokepoint diversions, capacity, demand, port congestion, tariffs front-running.

rubric.normal: Drewry World Container Index < $2,500/FEU and 1-month change < +30%.
